newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total sales up 24.7 percent, outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Total sales up 24.7 percent, outlook mixed.

text.p: French oil group Total SA said on Wednesday that its sales over the first nine months of the year were up by 24.7 percent and added that the outlook for the rest of the year was mixed.
Total said in a statement that its sales increased to 125.41 billion francs against 100.59 billion last year.

This was due to a more favourable environment compared to last year with the price of Brent crude 15 percent higher at $19.68 per barrel, an equal 15 percent rise in European refining margins to $12.2 per tonne while the French franc-to-dollar exchange rate improved slightly to 5.10 francs from 5.01 francs.
Higher hydrocarbons production, trading activity and refined product sales also helped while chemicals sales were up due to external growth at the Hutchinson HUTP.PA unit and in paints.

Total's upstream sales advanced to 8.32 billion francs from 7.04 billion, downstream sales surged to 98.30 billion from 76.80 billion while sales at chemicals rose to 18.42 billion from 16.51 billion francs.
Total said that the year-end operating environment featured a relatively strong Brent crude price and higher, albeit volatile, refining margins.
On the other hand, it said that European marketing margins had been under pressure from higher refined product prices.
It said hydrocarbons production was maintained at the first half 1996 level, a strong increase versus the 1995 level.
